text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: *Incident opened* SEV2 - Regional capacity dip (us-east-1) impacting inference latency/errors
Suspected: GPU capacity degradation / node churn
Primary symptoms: elevated p99, intermittent 5xx from router
Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/overload-throttling-and-priority-routing-response
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/hot-route-protection/overview?var=region=us-east-1

Sean Gallagher: seeing alerts from burn-rate + latency in us-east-1. Can someone confirm if this is *capacity dip* vs retry storm? Also need to confirm enterprise lane is actually protecting top routes.

Rafael Mendes: On it. I’m looking at router metrics now. p99 for chat/completions spiking to ~7-9s in us-east-1. 5xx rate ~0.6% for ~6 mins. Queue depth climbing.

Aisha Bello: From the hot-route dashboard (us-east-1):
- `lane_utilization{lane="enterprise"}` ~0.92
- `lane_utilization{lane="standard"}` ~0.98 and oscillating
- `throttled_count` jumped mostly on standard/self-serve.
Enterprise throttles are low but *not zero* (small bump ~30 rps). Might be from a couple enterprise tenants hitting per-route limit.

Sergio Costa: Alert context: `router_enterprise_lane_p95_latency > 1200ms` for 5m fired. We’re at ~1.6s now. Standard lane p95 ~2.8s.

Mina Haddad: Smart routing side: I see `capacity_signal=degraded` for us-east-1 (prefill saturation). Router is honoring lane split but we’re close to max. I can raise enterprise reservation for the top hot routes but that will push more shedding to standard.

Lauren Bishop: For this incident we should prioritize contractual enterprise endpoints. If we need to shed standard/self-serve, do it. Which enterprise routes are still impacted?

Rafael Mendes: Checking top enterprise routes list. In us-east-1, top offenders (latency) appear to be:
- `/v1/chat/completions` for tenant `acme-finance` route tag `chat-prod`
- `/v1/embeddings` for `northstar` (less critical)
`acme-finance` p95 in enterprise lane is ~1.9s (SLO 1.2s), availability OK.

Sean Gallagher: Can we validate lane isolation? i.e. is enterprise queue depth stable while standard explodes?

Aisha Bello: Queue depth split looks like:
- `queue_depth{lane="enterprise"}` peaked ~180, now 140
- `queue_depth{lane="standard"}` peaked ~1.8k, now 1.2k
So enterprise is *bounded* but still elevated.

Sofia Ivanova: Runtime signal: we had ~14% of GPUs in us-east-1 drop out over ~10 mins (node maintenance + a couple kernel restarts). Scheduler shows `decode_saturation` elevated (not purely prefill). Likely transient capacity loss, not a client retry storm.

Connor O'Brien: Release calendar shows no planned rollouts in us-east-1 right now. No active canaries for router. So this is infra/runtime capacity.

Sean Gallagher: OK. Mitigation path:
1) Increase shedding for standard + self-serve
2) Consider cross-region spillover for standard (us-west-2) if safe
3) Keep enterprise lane steady or bump reservation slightly
Mina, can you propose a minimal change that protects enterprise without completely starving standard?

Mina Haddad: Suggest:
- Increase enterprise reservation from 25% -> 35% for `chat-prod` tagged routes in us-east-1
- Enable stricter admission control for standard when `queue_depth_standard > 900` (currently 1200)
This should keep enterprise p95 down while we ride out GPU recovery.

Amara Diallo: Gateway side looks healthy. Rate limiting doing its job. 429s increased for self-serve as expected. Headers are correct (`Retry-After` present). Example from logs:
```
status=429 tenant=selfserve-*** route=/v1/chat/completions region=us-east-1
reason=over_capacity lane=standard retry_after=2 request_id=req_9b3...
```
No unusual 5xx at gateway.

Nikhil Sharma: If we’re changing reservation, please make sure customer-facing impact is consistent: standard gets 429 with Retry-After. No weird 500s. Also please note: Hosted API docs say clients should backoff on 429 (exponential + jitter).

Rafael Mendes: I can apply the policy via config (feature flag already on for us-east-1). Need confirmation: are we OK to bump enterprise reservation now?

Lauren Bishop: Yes. Protect enterprise. We can accept increased 429s for standard during incident.

Talia Benson: +1. Please capture what we changed and link it back to hot-route protection learnings.

Rafael Mendes: Applying config change now.
- Policy: `enterprise_reservation_pct` 0.25 -> 0.35 for `route_tag=chat-prod` in us-east-1
- Standard shed threshold `queue_depth_standard` 1200 -> 900
ETA 2-3 mins to propagate.

incident-bot: Change detected: `capacity-protection-policy` updated by Rafael Mendes (us-east-1)
Diff summary: reservation_pct +0.10, standard_shed_threshold -300
Config propagation: in_progress

Emily Zhao: FYI propagation delay last week was ~90s median, ~4m p99. Watch for inconsistent behavior across AZs.

Aisha Bello: Metrics now (2 mins post-change):
- Enterprise p95 dropping 1.6s -> 1.2s
- Standard 429 rate increased (expected) 3% -> 11%
- 5xx decreasing 0.6% -> 0.2%
This looks like the lane is doing what we want.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Let’s also confirm GPU pool recovery in us-east-1. Sofia, do we expect nodes back soon?

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler shows capacity stabilizing; we’ve regained ~6% GPUs already. Remaining restarts should complete within ~15-20 mins. Decode saturation trending down.

Sergio Costa: Alerts: burn-rate still elevated but no longer paging threshold. I’m going to annotate the dashboard with the config change timestamp.

Rafael Mendes: One more thing: `acme-finance` still has slight p99 > SLO (p99 ~2.8s). But availability is fine. I’ll keep an eye; might resolve as GPUs come back.

Sean Gallagher: Ack. Any customer comms needed?

Lauren Bishop: If `acme-finance` p99 stays elevated >10 mins, we should proactively notify their TAM (Liam) with “regional capacity dip, enterprise lane preserved availability, latency elevated, mitigation in place.”

Rafael Mendes: Agreed. Holding for now. Will update if p99 doesn’t recover.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Status update: us-east-1 router errors trending down; throttling primarily on standard lane. Next update in 15m.

Aisha Bello: 10m later: enterprise p95 980ms, p99 1.7s. Standard lane still throttling ~8-10% but stable. Queue depth enterprise back under 100.

Sean Gallagher: Nice. Let’s keep the reservation bump until fleet is fully recovered, then revert to baseline and write this up as “policy worked; propagation ok; consider lowering standard shed threshold default for us-east-1.”

Talia Benson: Please drop the notes + graphs into the weekly hot-route protection doc after we close. Also we should follow up on Emily’s point—config propagation p99 still too high for incident response.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. I’ll start drafting a quick incident note + action items once we declare resolved.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: *Incident mitigated* - metrics within normal range (enterprise lane p95 < 1.1s, 5xx < 0.1%).
Owner: Rafael Mendes
Follow-ups: add action items in postmortems channel + link dashboards/annotations.
